positioning: A nose with a dog attached, and no off switch.
story: The Beagle is mostly nose. The rest of the dog is there to carry it.
English hunters bred the breed to follow rabbits on foot. A pack worked together, heads down, voices up. The AKC recognized the Beagle in 1885.
That nose holds around 220 million scent receptors. A person has about six million. Give a Beagle a trail and the rest of the world disappears.
It still works for a living. The USDA Beagle Brigade sniffs out smuggled fruit and meat in airport baggage. The breed was chosen for the nose, and for a face no traveler minds meeting.
Fame came too. Snoopy made the silhouette a star. Uno won Best in Show at Westminster in 2008, the first Beagle ever to do it. Miss P won it again in 2015.
Living with one means living with the nose. A Beagle on a scent is deaf to you. It needs a fence, patience, and a latched pantry.
fblocks: Likely from the old French begueule, a loud mouth, or the Celtic beag, small. Either fits.
Snoopy, the world’s best-known cartoon dog. Uno, Best in Show at Westminster in 2008. Miss P, in 2015.
The nose rules the dog. Off leash, a Beagle follows a trail over the horizon. Needs a fence, company, and watching at mealtimes.
The USDA Beagle Brigade screens airport baggage for food and contraband. A world-class nose and a face too friendly to alarm anyone.
Recognized by the AKC in 1885. About six puppies to a litter. A top-ten American breed for most of the last century.
days: Morning sun, an open screen door, and an old hound with a well-earned nap.
A Beagle has about 220 million scent receptors. You have around six million.
Uno won Westminster in 2008 and bayed at the crowd all the way around the ring.
The USDA Beagle Brigade finds smuggled fruit in airport suitcases.
Every storm ends. Sit by the door and keep your nose ready.
Legend says Queen Elizabeth I kept tiny pocket beagles, small enough for a saddlebag.
A gentle hand on an old head, and a porch swing that keeps the rhythm.
last_walk:
The rain taps the window, and the lamp is low.
A Beagle ends the day curled close to its oldest friend. The nose finally rests. The tail finally stills. Outside, the town is damp and quiet. Inside, two dogs and a blanket make a small, warm world.
